task.title: Bind the watcher socket in a private directory on Linux
task.description:
The sync watcher prefers a socket path in the system temporary directory, which on Linux is world-writable /tmp, and the hardened per-user directory the code already implements is never reached.

candidatePaths tries os.TempDir() first, userTempDir() second, and .git/workbook/ third, taking the first candidate that fits maxSocketPath of 100 bytes (internal/syncloop/socket.go:108-135). userTempDir carefully validates owner, mode, and symlink status of /tmp/workbook-<uid> (socket.go:141-162) and is then never used, because /tmp/wb-<16 hex>.sock is 29 bytes and always fits. On darwin os.TempDir() is the per-user $TMPDIR, so darwin is safe by accident; on Linux it is /tmp.

The socket name is sha256(abs(commonGitDir))[:8], so it is predictable to anyone who can guess the repository path. On a shared Linux host or CI box another local user can pre-bind /tmp/wb-<hash>.sock and listen. bind dials the path first and returns ErrWatcherLive if anything answers (internal/syncloop/server.go:42-45), so every `workbook sync --watch` and the watcher inside `workbook serve` then refuse to start with "a Workbook watcher already owns this repository", permanently. Cleanup also fails, because os.Remove cannot unlink another users file in a sticky /tmp. This is a durable denial of the whole sync optimization behind a misleading error, not a takeover: clients rendezvous through .git/workbook/watcher.json, which the attacker cannot write.

Separately, bind chmods the socket to 0600 only after net.Listen creates it (server.go:49-56). With the usual umask 022 the interim mode is 0755, which denies connect, so this is normally harmless, but under umask 0 the socket is briefly world-connectable. Anything that connects can drive status, which leaks repository error strings, task IDs, and the watcher PID, and ack, which silently drops a recorded conflict so it is never reported to a human (server.go:86-97).

Both ends of the watcher protocol also read a line with no size limit: server.go:76 and client.go:89 both use bufio ReadBytes with only a 5s deadline as a bound.

Acceptance:
- The private per-user directory is preferred over os.TempDir(), or os.TempDir() is dropped on non-darwin platforms.
- A candidate path in a world-writable directory is treated as unusable.
- The socket is created so that it is never world-connectable, by binding inside a 0700 directory or by setting umask around the listen.
- Both protocol readers bound the line length.
- A test asserts the chosen path is not world-writable on Linux.
